To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the design of the domestic policy will likely be the key determinant of emissions trading's effectiveness in transition economies; (2) the revenue from the sale of emissions will be a key consideration in the design of domestic systems, and (3) the revenue will likely be used in one of three ways: general government revenue, private sector investment, or carbon mitigation investment.
the benefits of emissions trading are greatest when it is combined with domestic policies that encourage further emission reductions.
the potential benefits of international emissions trading are great, and that the design of domestic systems in seller nations will be crucial to realizing those benefits.

a domestic policy that combines a carbon tax and a carbon mitigation fund would be the most effective policy for transition economies.

the design of domestic emissions trading systems is a key determinant of the effectiveness of international emissions trading.
